name: Terrain Multiresolution Representation
aliases: Terrain Multiresolution Representation — Bintree hierarchy with 4-8 subdivision, Regular grid connectivity patches
definition: A multiresolution terrain representation using a bintree hierarchy formed by 4-8 subdivision (longest edge bisection), where each node represents a patch of triangles. The patch interior uses regular grid connectivity with n rows of triangles, allowing n to be any integer (not just power of two). Each patch has V = (n + 1)(n + 2)/2 vertices and T = n^2 triangles. Terrain dimensions are limited to (2mn + 1)^2 for non-negative integer m.
summary: Terrain Multiresolution Representation is a view-dependent LOD method using Binary Triangle Trees to adaptively refine terrain meshes by longest-edge bisection, ensuring continuous, crack-free rendering.
